MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 6, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:04 p.m., on January 6, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 20, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

City Council Minutes  1  January 6, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member Ury
arrived at 6:42 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council unanimously approved the City's
commencement of litigation against the State of California Department of Finance. This will be
the 3rd or 4th required challenge of the State for its denial of the City's Recognized Obligation
Payments Schedule (ROPS.) Mr. Curley noted that State law requires cities to put in writing their
requests for reimbursement of funding to carry out the ongoing components of the former
redevelopment agencies. The State, every 6 months, receives these requests for payment from
local agencies and they deny the majority of requests across the board. Mr. Curley said that the
State has rejected approximately one half million dollars of Mission Viejo's requested
reimbursement and there are more than 150 lawsuits regarding this type of denial. Staff believes
that the grounds are very clear in that the State approved the City doing what it did but then
denied reimbursement for those pre-approved actions. The administrative record is very
favorable to the City and staff will continue to try to recover the monies administratively with
litigation being a last resort. Mr. Curley noted that the State doesn't take these claims seriously
until a City actually sues them and once sued, the Attorney General hears the case and usually
approves payment. In summary, Mr. Curley reiterated that the Council wishes to recover the
City's half million dollars and to do so quickly and at a low cost.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Greg Raths, M.V.: introduced himself as a candidate for the U.S. House of Representatives 45th
Congressional District. Mr. Raths stated that he can be trusted and when elected, he will report
back to the leaders and citizens of Mission Viejo what is going on in Washington.

Kay Kearny, representing McCormick Ambulance Services, Garden Grove: announced that she
heard that the City's current ambulance provider cannot pay its employees and may be halting
service. She stated that McCormick stands ready to step in and serve the City if called upon.

Joe Chidley, CEO of McCormick Ambulance Services, Irvine: offered his company's service to
the City of Mission Viejo should the need arise.

Helen Workun, M.V.: thanked the City Council Members for making Mission Viejo a very
desirable place to live. She stated that she is proud of her City any time of year but it's nice to be
in this beautiful and magical place during the holidays. She also thanked the City's hard working
and creative staff.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he has not heard any discussion about issuing an RFP for
legal services in the past two years and he thinks it is long overdue. Mr. Wontrobski expressed
concern with some recent incidents at the YMCA involving a homeless person who sleeps in the
parking lot and uses the facilities. He stated that he is worried about the safety of the YMCA
members and staff and he recommended that the Sheriff's Department get involved.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

22. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at various events in the month of December
including ribbon cutting ceremonies at Sola Salon and Nekter Juice Bar and the grand reopening
of Contours Image Center. She also attended the Animal Services Center holiday party, a
birthday party for resident Madeline Rapp Buss who is 100 years old, the Giovanni holiday
spectacular concert, a Muslim Heritage Celebration and the Newhart School Character Forum.
Council Member Reardon also reported on her attendance at the City's employee holiday
luncheon and Admiral Bill Miles' 99th birthday celebration. Mr. Miles, a veteran pilot, was shot
down not once but twice and he is just an amazing human being with a great story. Council
Member Reardon announced that she took 23 children to the bear project at Kaleidoscope center
where they are hosting the bear project rent free. Artists Joy Aldridge and Aileen May open the
shop on Fridays and Saturdays from 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and work with residents to place
mosaic tiles on the fiberglass bears. There are 9 bears in total, each with different themes and the
community can participate in the artwork project. Council Member Reardon reminded residents
that the City is collecting toys for NEGU Joy Jars and since the collection efforts were light over
the holidays, the project has been extended to January 17, 2014. Lastly, Council Member
Reardon asked the City Attorney if he would bring back the City's retention policy and the
Information Technology policy for discussion and possible changes.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht commented on the discussion of item 24 at the December 2, 2013,
City Council Meeting. She noted that she wants the public record to be complete and she will
admit some more data on Crime Survivors and Crime Stoppers. Council Member Schlicht stated
that the record should reflect that Wendy Bucknum sits on the board of both Crime Stoppers and

City Council Minutes  12  January 6, 2014
 Crime Survivors and she feels it was unethical for Mrs. Bucknum to vote for funding for
numerous organizations that she is associated with. She further stated that Mission Viejo is
becoming more and more of a private playground with public funds and there is too much
influence by staff, special interests, vendors and contractors. Council Member Schlicht said that
she wants to give authority back to the City's Committees and Commissions for input, debate,
discussion and discovery. She also discussed the Common Core education program and stated
that government is becoming too central in our lives. She encouraged parents to learn about the
controversial program which 15 states are now considering withdrawing from. She stated that it
takes parents authority away and she was surprised to learn that the Common Core Curriculum is
backed by Bill Gates. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from
Thomas Holcroft: "To prevent inquiry is among the worst of evils."

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he attended the character program at Newhart School and it
was very eye opening. The presenters throw hypothetical questions out to the students and it was
interesting to see the ethical dilemmas that are before kids today. Council Member Ury noted
that he had a great Christmas and holiday season and he looks forward to a fun 2014.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness shared a short video of the new service club placard board which
completes the intersection at La Paz and Marguerite.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked Rhonda Reardon for her service as Mayor in 2013. She stated that the
Council Members all sacrifice money and family time while serving on the Council but Council
Member Reardon really went above and beyond in representing the City last year. Mayor Kelley
noted that she helped with the planning of the character program at Newhart Middle School
which has been offered to all four of the City's middle schools. The program provides a forum
for the kids to hear and discuss ethical dilemmas and the pilot event went really well with about
100 students participating. She agreed with Council Member Ury that it was really eye-opening
to learn what our kids are exposed to now. Mayor Kelley noted that the program was developed
by Russ Williams of the Passkey Foundation who presented the ethical scenarios with Council
Members, the Police Chief, the Division Fire Chief, the City Manager and several other
volunteers serving as table mentors. The next program will be at Los Alisos Intermediate School
in January or February. Mayor Kelley announced that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
did another excellent job with Santa's arrival and Workshop. The lights were beautiful and she
received many comments from residents and outsiders alike. She thanked Assistant City
Manager Rattay and his staff for the civic center lighting as well. Mayor Kelley announced that
there will be a Blood Drive on January 17 from 12 noon to 6:15 p.m. and she encouraged
residents to register on the Red Cross website or to call her for an appointment. She also
announced that the City will be providing a room at City Hall for the Veterans of Foreign Wars
to counsel veterans on their benefits every Wednesday morning beginning January 8. Those
City Council Minutes  13  January 6, 2014
 interested can contact her or visit the City's blog for more information. Lastly, Mayor Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of January is perseverance
which is a good reminder as we start a new year.
